blocks.source: Vol III, Test-Time Compute, § Three Axes of Test-Time Compute
blocks.md: Giving a repair agent a four-thousand-token allowance does not determine its latency, memory footprint, or diagnostic reach, because the runtime can spend those same four thousand tokens on one long derivation, four parallel candidate patches, or three edit–test–revise rounds. Although all three options can consume the same number of output tokens, they stress the serving system in different ways. A long derivation generates tokens one after another along a single causal chain. Independent candidate patches can run concurrently across accelerator hardware.

questions.q: The section **Three Axes of Test-Time Compute** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: pass@k = 1-(1-p)^k caps any selector that returns an unchanged pool member, while realized accuracy is set by the selector, so coverage near 98 percent can coexist with a vote that plateaus near half.
A step check that rejects a fraction r of b children gives an effective branching factor b(1-r), so a tree stays finite on its own only when r > 1-1/b and otherwise needs hard caps.
Test-time compute is a per-decision allowance that sets the attempt cost in C_eff, so it pays only when it raises acceptance faster than cost, and difficulty should route the budget.
Depth, breadth, and feedback can spend the same output ceiling yet differ in critical path, retained KV state, and bill, and only feedback adds information the prompt and weights lack.
